_comment: The SCA twin of unsupported-dependency: the same file: path, in the archive the reviewer builds from. A source review reads its dependencies from the committed package-lock.json, which records the install as a link to ../shared/helper - outside the source root, so the archive does not hold it and it cannot be reviewed. The diagnosis is the XPI one - nothing identifies a local path - and the finding anchors at the lock entry. This submission is the one npm actually installs from, so its response keeps the lock-file route the XPI branch must not offer, and asks for the library in the archive rather than bundled into the add-on. The XPI here also ships a package.json of its own, which in a source-code submission belongs in the archive - the copy the reviewer reads and the build installs from - so sca-xpi-declares-vendoring reports it, naming the file(s) on the finding. It narrows nothing here - the archive is still reviewed in full.
